q: 1. The type of projection in which the surface are equally foreshortened is
explain: In isometric projection all three principal edges/axes of an object are foreshortened equally (by the same isometric ratio, ~0.816), unlike oblique or other projections where foreshortening differs by direction.

q: 2. In comparison to an isometric projection, the appearance of an isometric view is
explain: An isometric projection uses the reduced isometric scale (~0.816 of true length), while an isometric view/drawing is plotted using true (actual) lengths, making the isometric view appear larger than the true isometric projection.

q: 3. On isometric plane, a circle appears as
explain: Since isometric planes are inclined to the viewer, a circle lying on any isometric plane is foreshortened in one direction and appears as an ellipse.

q: 4. While making isometric projections the ellipse is preferably drawn by
explain: The four-center (approximate) method is the standard, quick way to construct isometric ellipses using arcs struck from four centers, giving a close approximation to the true ellipse.

q: 5. Isometric projection cannot be drawn by
explain: Isometric projections are commonly constructed using the box method, coordinate method, or offset method; the 'zone method' is not a recognized technique for isometric drawing (it is instead associated with development of surfaces, e.g., sphere development).

q: 6. A sphere in isometric projection appears as a circle of diameter
options: equal to the diameter of sphere
greater than the diameter of sphere
explain: In isometric projection (using the true isometric scale), a sphere projects as a circle whose diameter equals the sphere's actual diameter, since the same foreshortening ratio applies equally in every direction on a sphere.

q: 7. Drawing equipment used by draftsmen primarily as a guide for drawing horizontal lines on a drafting table is
explain: The T-square's blade slides along the working edge of the drawing board, providing a reliable guide for drawing horizontal lines.

q: 8. The area of bathroom shall not be less than
explain: As per building bye-law/National Building Code norms used in these standards, the minimum area prescribed for a bathroom is 1.8 m².

q: 9. Maximum distance between black board and last row of benches should not be more than ...... in school buildings.
explain: School building design norms specify a maximum blackboard-to-last-bench distance of 7 m to ensure visibility for all students.

q: 10. The geometrical name of the curvature of the coil used in spiral binding is
explain: The spiral binding coil does not correspond to any of the standard mathematical spiral curves (Archimedean, logarithmic) or an involute; hence the answer is 'none of these'.

q: 11. Which of the following methods is not used for drawing elliptical curves?
explain: Ellipses are commonly constructed by the intersecting-arcs, concentric-circles, or oblong (rectangle) methods; there is no standard 'tangent method' for drawing an ellipse.

q: 12. Projection of an object shown by three views is known as
explain: Multiview (orthographic) projection represents an object using multiple related views (typically front, top, and side) obtained by projecting perpendicularly onto mutually perpendicular planes.

q: 13. In orthographic projection, the elevation is obtained on a plane called
explain: The elevation (front view) of an object is obtained by projecting it onto the Vertical Plane (VP).

q: 14. In multiview projections, the XY line is also known as
explain: The XY line, which represents the intersection of the horizontal plane (HP) and vertical plane (VP), is commonly called the reference line.

q: 15. In first angle projection method, the relative positions of the object, plane and observers are
options: may be placed in any order
explain: In first angle projection, the sequence is Observer → Object → Plane of Projection, so the object lies between the observer and the plane.

q: 16. In first angle projection system, the right hand side view of an object is drawn
explain: In first-angle projection, each view is projected onto the plane behind the object and then folded into position, which places the right-side view on the left of the front view (elevation).

q: 17. If the front view of an object exhibits width and height, then what dimensions of an object are exhibited by a right side view?
explain: The front view shows width and height; the side view, being a projection along the width direction, shows the depth (length) and height of the object.

q: 18. For orthographic projections, B.I.S. recommends the following
explain: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS/IS codes) recommends first angle projection as the standard method for orthographic drawings in India.

q: 19. The recommended symbol for indicating the angle of projection shows two views of the frustum of a
explain: The standard projection symbol (as per BIS/ISO) is drawn using two views of a truncated cone (frustum of a cone), distinguishing first-angle from third-angle projection by the arrangement of the circle and its projection.

q: 20. The line joining the front and top views of a point is called
explain: The vertical line connecting the front view (elevation) and the top view (plan) of a point, perpendicular to the XY line, is called a projector.

q: 21. A point lying in the HP, has its top view above XY line. Its front view will be
explain: A point lying exactly in the Horizontal Plane (HP) has zero distance above VP, so its front view always lies on the XY (reference) line, regardless of where the top view is.

q: 22. A point whose elevation and plan are above XY, is situated in
explain: If both the front view (above XY, meaning in front of VP is reversed logic) and top view lie above the XY line, the point lies in the second dihedral angle (above HP and behind VP).

q: 23. Site plan shows
explain: A site plan is a plan view of the plot showing the location and orientation of the building(s) on the site along with surrounding features such as roads and boundaries.

q: 24. In which of the following projection, the observer is at finite distance from the object?
explain: In perspective projection, the observer's eye (station point) is at a finite distance from the object, causing convergence of projectors to vanishing points, unlike orthographic/isometric/oblique projections which assume the observer is at infinity (parallel projectors).

q: 25. A building drawing consists of
explain: A complete building drawing set includes the site plan, floor plans, elevations, sections, and foundation details, so 'all of these' is correct.

q: 26. When the picture plane coincide with the object, the perspective of the object will be of its
explain: If the picture plane passes through the object itself, the perspective projection of that portion coincides with the object, so it appears at its actual (same) size.

q: 27. In the first angle method of orthographic projection
options: the object comes between the observer and the plane
the plane comes between the object and observer
the observer comes between the object and the plane
explain: First angle projection places the object between the observer's eye and the plane of projection (Observer → Object → Plane).

q: 28. The purpose of sectional view is to show the
explain: A sectional view is created by imagining the object cut by a plane to reveal and clarify hidden internal features that are not visible in a normal view.

q: 29. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw
explain: A parallel ruling straight-edge is a drafting machine attachment that slides vertically on wires/cords while remaining horizontal, used primarily to draw horizontal parallel lines.

q: 30. The locus of a point is a ............. when in moves in a plane in such a way that its distance ............. a fixed line is always a constant.
explain: A point that maintains a constant perpendicular distance from a fixed straight line traces another straight line parallel to it.

q: 31. The ratio of the shortest distance from the focus to the shortest distance from the directrix is called
explain: Eccentricity is defined as the ratio of the distance of a point on a conic from the focus to its distance from the directrix; this ratio determines whether the conic is an ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola.

q: 32. In case of aligned method of dimensioning, they can be readable form .............
options: bottoms and right side of drawing sheet
bottoms and left side of drawing sheet
bottoms and top side of drawing sheet
explain: In the aligned system, dimensions are placed so they can be read from the bottom edge and the right-hand edge of the drawing sheet.

q: 33. Scales for architectural and building drawings for plan is generally taken as .............
explain: Building plans are conventionally drawn at a scale of 1:100, which balances readable detail with manageable sheet size for typical buildings.

q: 34. Normally perspective projection is used by .............
explain: Perspective drawings, because they give a realistic, eye-view appearance of a finished project, are commonly used by manufacturers and marketers for promotional/presentation purposes.

q: 35. The edge of the board on which T-square is made to slide is called .............
explain: The left (or designated) straight edge of the drawing board, along which the T-square's stock slides, is called the working edge.

q: 36. A drafter helps in drawing .............
explain: A drafter (drafting machine) is designed mainly to draw parallel and perpendicular lines quickly and accurately using its scale arms set at fixed angles.

q: 37. In the engineering system of paper sizes, which of the following is "A2" size?
38. Which of the following pencil leads is hardest?
explain: On the pencil grading scale, 'H' denotes hardness (higher H numbers = harder); among HB, H, B, F, the H grade is the hardest listed.

q: 39. To lay off an angle from a given line, what marks on the protractor should you align for a higher accuracy?
explain: For accurate angle layout, the protractor's center mark must be aligned with the vertex of the angle, and the 0°–180° baseline aligned with the reference line, so all three (0°, 180°, and center) marks are used together.

q: 40. To draw smooth curves of any nature, drafting instrument used is .............
explain: A French curve is a flexible-shaped template specifically designed to help draw smooth irregular curves that are not simple arcs of a circle.

q: 41. Parallel lines can be drawn with the help of .............
explain: Parallel lines can be drawn using a mini-drafter, a T-square (sliding along the board edge), or a pair of set squares (one sliding against the other), so all listed tools work.

q: 42. A typical layout of drawing sheet do not contain .............
explain: Standard drawing sheet layouts include centering marks, orientation marks, and identification/title marks, but 'trimming marks' are not part of the standard sheet layout elements defined by drawing standards.

q: 43. Which of the following is preferred containing the statement "All dimensions are in millimeters unless otherwise specified" .............
explain: General notes such as the units statement are conventionally placed within the title block of the drawing sheet.

q: 44. "A" series of paper has length of width ratio of approximately .............
explain: ISO A-series paper sizes maintain a constant aspect ratio of √2:1, which allows each size to be halved into the next smaller size while preserving the same proportions.

q: 45. Number of orientation mark generally contained by a drawing sheet is .............
explain: A standard drawing sheet layout generally includes two orientation marks to indicate the correct viewing direction of the sheet.

q: 46. Extension arm used with engineering compass facilitates .............
options: to draw circles of larger diameter
to adjust distance between the legs
explain: An extension (lengthening) bar attached to a compass increases its radius reach, allowing the drafter to draw circles of larger diameter than the compass alone permits.

q: 47. To facilitate extension, entries in the table should begin form .............
explain: Tables designed for future additions are conventionally filled starting from the bottom row upward, leaving room to extend entries above as needed.

q: 48. The nature of surface of sphere is .............
explain: A sphere's surface is curved in two independent directions simultaneously (both meridian and latitude directions), making it a doubly curved surface, unlike a cylinder or cone which are singly curved.

q: 49. If a semicircular thin sheet is folded to form a cone, then the front view of the cone appears as .............
explain: A semicircular development folded into a cone (where the semicircle's radius becomes the cone's slant height) produces a cone whose front view is an equilateral triangle, a special geometric relationship between the semicircle and the resulting cone's proportions.

q: 50. The intersection of a cone by a plane results in .............
explain: By definition, curves obtained by intersecting a cone with a plane (circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola, triangle) are collectively called conic sections.

q: 51. The curve of intersection of any solid with a line is .............
explain: A line, being one-dimensional, intersects the surface of a solid at discrete points (entry/exit points), not along a line or loop.

q: 52. When a cylinder penetrates into a vertical cone with their axes parallel to each other, the top view of the curve of intersection is .............
explain: When the penetrating cylinder's axis is parallel (coincident in direction) with the cone's vertical axis, the intersection curve, seen in the top view, projects as a circle.

q: 53. When a vertical cylinder is penetrated by a horizontal cylinder, the top view of the curve of intersection is .............
explain: The intersection of a vertical cylinder with a horizontal cylinder of different diameter produces a curve that, in the top view, appears as an elliptical arc.

q: 54. In full sectional view, the object is imagined to be cut off .............
explain: A full section is obtained by passing a cutting plane completely through the object, conceptually removing (cutting away) one half of it to reveal the interior.

q: 55. Axonometric projection is a special type of .............
explain: Axonometric projection (which includes isometric, dimetric, and trimetric) is a category of orthographic (parallel) projection in which the object is tilted relative to the projection plane to show multiple faces at once.

q: 56. In the cabinet projection, an angle at which the projectors meet the plane of projection is .............
explain: Cabinet projection is an oblique projection drawn with receding lines at 30° (some texts use 45°) to reduce distortion, while depth is drawn at half scale; per this reference the receiving angle is taken as 30°.

q: 57. While making cavalier projections the ellipse is preferably drawn by .............
explain: In cavalier (and other oblique) projections, circular features on the receding faces are typically constructed using the oblong (rectangle-based) method to plot the true elliptical shape.

q: 58. The natural details are presented on .............
explain: A topographic map depicts natural features (relief, rivers, vegetation, contours) of the terrain, whereas a cadastral map primarily shows property/ownership boundaries.

q: 59. Free hand sketches are used for expressing and recording .............
explain: Freehand sketches are a quick way to record and communicate a concept or new idea before it is developed into a formal, scaled drawing.

q: 60. In sketching, horizontal lines are draw from .............
explain: For right-handed drafters, the natural and recommended direction for sketching horizontal lines freehand is left to right, for better control and visibility of the line being drawn.
